questions.question: Which middleware does getDefaultMiddleware() include in a production build?
options: Thunk, immutability check and serializability check
questions.explanation: The action creator, immutability and serializability checks are development-only. In production only the thunk middleware remains.

questions.question: What is the recommended way to add a custom logger middleware while keeping the defaults?
questions.explanation: middleware must be a callback. Using the Tuple's concat keeps the defaults (including thunk) and preserves TypeScript types; passing an array throws an error.

questions.question: You dispatch an action whose payload is a `new Date()`. What happens in development with default settings?
options: The store throws and the action is discarded
The Date is automatically converted to an ISO string
Nothing; Dates are allowed in Redux
The serializability middleware logs a warning about a non-serializable value
questions.explanation: The serializability check warns (it does not throw) about non-serializable values in actions and state. The usual fix is to store an ISO string instead.

questions.question: Why might you set `devTools: process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production"`?
options: Redux DevTools cannot connect to production builds anyway
devTools defaults to true, so users with the extension could inspect sensitive production state
It is required for the thunk middleware to work in production
It turns off the immutability check
questions.explanation: configureStore enables DevTools by default in every environment. Disabling it in production stops anyone with the extension from browsing your app's state.
